title: Adding up only the ones that match
idea: Combine the accumulator (review from u41) with an if in a loop: sum only the values that pass a test. This is 'total of the ones that match the rule'.

exercises.prompt: To answer 'what's the sum of the even numbers from 1 to 10?', what combines?
options: An accumulator AND an if inside the loop
exercises.explanation: The if picks the even values; the accumulator adds only those. Together they sum the matches.
Evens 1 to 10 are 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Their sum: 2+4+6+8+10 = 30. total += i runs only when even.

exercises.prompt: Where must total += i go to sum only the matches?
options: Inside the if (two levels of indent)
exercises.explanation: Inside the if, total += i runs only when the condition is true, so it sums just the matching values.

exercises.prompt: If total += i were at level ONE instead of inside the if, what would it sum (range(1, 11))?
options: All numbers 1 to 10 = 55, ignoring the condition
exercises.explanation: At level one it adds every i, summing all of 1 to 10 (55). The if's filter is lost. Indentation decides what's summed.

exercises.prompt: total = 0 still goes before the loop when summing conditionally.
exercises.explanation: Yes. Initialize once before; the if just decides which values to add, not where the total starts.
Odds 1 to 10: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. Sum: 25. Flipping the test to == 1 sums the odds instead.

exercises.prompt: Arrange code to sum the even numbers from 1 to 6.
exercises.explanation: Initialize total, loop, test even, add i inside the if, print after. Result: 2+4+6 = 12.
Evens 1 to 6: 2, 4, 6. Sum: 12. The accumulator adds only the matching values.

exercises.prompt: What's the difference between counting matches and summing matches?
options: Count adds 1 per match; sum adds the value i per match
exercises.explanation: Inside the if, count += 1 counts how many match; total += i sums their values. The if is the same; what you add differs.

exercises.prompt: Re-check: sum the multiples of 3 from 1 to 10. Which values are added, and what's the total?
exercises.explanation: if i % 3 == 0 picks 3, 6, 9; total += i sums them to 18. The combined pattern generalizes to any rule.
